title: Starlight Medical Private VPC Discovery
summary: Discovery for Private (VPC) deployment. Starlight Medical needs private connectivity, EU data residency, SOC2-level auditability, and low-latency targets for clinical assistant. Discussed VPC peering vs PrivateLink, route table requirements, egress restrictions, and pilot benchmarks. Agreed next steps: share architecture doc, pricing for Dedicated vs Private, and schedule a tech deep dive with network team.
next_steps: Send Private deployment architecture doc and VPC peering runbook (Redwood)
Share pricing for Dedicated/reserved capacity and pilot pricing (Redwood)
Customer to provide network CIDRs, approved regions, and security requirements (Customer)
Schedule technical deep dive focused on VPC peering and PrivateLink with Starlight network team next week
action_items: Ethan Rivera: provide VPC peering checklist and sample CloudFormation templates by 2026-12-12
Priya Nair: share network CIDR ranges, max MTU, and egress firewall rules by 2026-12-09
Maya Chen: send pricing sheet and pilot agreement draft by 2026-12-08
Daniel Park: confirm KMS/HSM provider requirements and key rotation policy by 2026-12-11
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Rivera (Redwood SE), Jonas Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Starlight Head of Infra), Liam O'Connell (CTO), Daniel Park (Sec Eng), Aisha Khan (DevOps)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to understand network constraints and security requirements for private VPC deployment of Redwood inference; decide hosted vs dedicated vs private, evaluate peering vs private endpoints, region constraints.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining; quick intros — i'll kick off, i'm maya with redwood, and ethan and jonas from our infra team.
00:12 Priya Nair: hi all, priya here, head of infra at starlight. we've got liam and daniel on too. thanks.
00:18 Ethan Rivera: great, uh just to set expectations, we want to understand your network posture, regulatory constraints, and perf goals so we can recommend Hosted / Dedicated or Private.
00:35 Liam O'Connell: main thing for us: clinical assistant will hit PHI, so we need everything inside our VPC or in a customer-controlled network. EU data residency for a subset of patients, and we need SOC2-level audit logs.
00:50 Jonas Patel: understood — when you say "inside your VPC" do you mean peering or a private endpoint? both are options; they have different tradeoffs.
01:05 Priya Nair: yeah, we prefer VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink depending on performance. also interested in private endpoints to avoid any public egress.
01:18 Ethan Rivera: okay; quick rundown. Private deployment options: 1) VPC peering — you peer your VPC with our managed VPC, route tables and security groups handle traffic; 2) PrivateLink / Private endpoints — service endpoints into your VPC, often simpler for auth but needs ENIs and account limits; 3) Dedicated — reserved infra in our account but with more isolation, can be combined with VPC peering.
01:45 Liam O'Connell: latency is critical — sub 150ms p95 for 512-token prompts. can redwood guarantee that from eu-west-1 region?
01:58 Ethan Rivera: we measure region-to-region latency and can place private deployments in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 depending on availability. for clinical workloads we recommend eu-central-1 for lower latency to your infra, but we'll run benchmarks.
02:15 Daniel Park: security questions: KMS integration, HSM, key rotation, audit logs, SSO and RBAC, and network egress controls. can you integrate with our KMS?
02:28 Jonas Patel: yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM for encryption at rest; rotation policies can be aligned. audit logs are generated and shipped to your logging endpoint (we support syslog, S3, and partner SIEMs), but we'll need to check retention windows for your plan.
02:42 Priya Nair: when you say "shipped to our logging endpoint" is that across the peered link or via public egress? we can't have logs leaving the VPC over public internet.
02:55 Ethan Rivera: logs can be pushed over the peered link; they don't need to traverse the public internet. that said, depending on the integration (e.g., S3 cross-account), there are IAM roles and trust that we set up.
03:10 Aisha Khan: firewall constraints: we have strict egress — only certain IP ranges allowed and a proxy for outbound. can redwood sit behind our proxy or do you require direct connectivity?
03:24 Maya Chen: good question — for PrivateLink or peering we don't require public egress, but for Hosted API you'd need outbound access. For Private, we can operate entirely over peered connectivity or PrivateLink with no public egress.
03:40 Liam O'Connell: what about network address ranges? our infra team uses a lot of small /24s, we have overlapping ranges with some vendors. do you support NAT or SNAT on your side?
03:52 Ethan Rivera: we typically recommend non-overlapping CIDRs; if overlaps exist we can put a NAT gateway in the path or use a proxy-based solution, but that adds complexity. we'll provide a sample CloudFormation to show the patterns.
04:10 Daniel Park: compliance — can we get SOC2 report and penetration test summary? also ISO if you have it.
04:20 Jonas Patel: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 documentation we can share under an NDA. also we provide architecture diagrams and network runbooks for auditors.
04:33 Priya Nair: any constraints on region availability for Private? we need EU residency for certain datasets. do you deploy to eu-west-2?
04:45 Ethan Rivera: currently we have Private deployments available in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1; eu-west-2 is on our roadmap for Q1 next year. if eu-west-2 is a hard requirement we can discuss a migration path or regional restriction in the contract.
05:00 Liam O'Connell: fine, eu-central-1 acceptable for now. next: how do you handle autoscaling — we want predictable latency under burst?
05:13 Ethan Rivera: Redwood Dedicated supports reserved capacity with configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. For Private, we can provision reserved pools tied to your deployment with SLOs. autoscaling is orchestrated by our control plane but the data path remains in your VPC via peering or private endpoints.
05:30 Aisha Khan: what's the onboarding pilot look like? we want to run a 2-week pilot with our prompts and a small subset of traffic, also run regression checks.
05:42 Maya Chen: typical pilot: 2 weeks, we provision a small private deployment, run your evals, measure latency/cost, and iterate. we'll share a pilot checklist and a pricing sheet for pilot vs production.
05:55 Daniel Park: concern: key management — can you do HSM-backed keys via our HSM provider?
06:02 Jonas Patel: we integrate with common KMS/HSM providers and can support customer-managed HSMs in many setups; we'll need the specifics — vendor, connectivity, and any FIPS requirements.
06:16 Priya Nair: network ops question: do you require route propagation in our TGW or just static routes?
06:25 Ethan Rivera: static routes in route tables are typical for peering; for Transit Gateway we can support route propagation depending on your AWS config. we'll include both patterns in the runbook.
06:40 Liam O'Connell: are there any per-tenant quotas or ENI limits we should know about with PrivateLink?
06:48 Ethan Rivera: yes PrivateLink creates ENIs in your account; there are AWS limits — we provide guidance and can request quota increases as part of onboarding. peering avoids ENI limits but needs route management.
07:05 Aisha Khan: what about egress to 3rd-party endpoints like our EHR? can redwood call out to external services from within the private environment?
07:17 Jonas Patel: outbound calls to external services from the private deployment are possible but must be explicitly allowed and routed; we can use NAT or a dedicated proxy inside your VPC. we'll document the pattern.
07:30 Liam O'Connell: cost — what's the delta between Dedicated and Private?
07:35 Maya Chen: Dedicated is more like reserved capacity in our account with isolation and lower onboarding time; Private (VPC deploy) includes the private connectivity work and potentially higher setup, so pilot pricing differs. i'll send a detailed sheet after this call.
07:50 Daniel Park: any mention of other vendors we should consider? we're also talking to AWS Bedrock and OpenAI for embeddings/LLM API.
07:58 Maya Chen: understood — we'll highlight where Redwood provides deterministic latency and tooling for ops and cost controls.
08:10 Priya Nair: ok let's wrap with next steps and owners.
08:18 Maya Chen: recap: ethan will share VPC peering checklist + cloudformation; i'll send pricing and pilot agreement; priya you'll share CIDRs and security requirements. date-wise can we aim to have the tech deep dive the week of 2026-12-14?
08:34 Priya Nair: yes that works. we'll target 2026-12-15 for the deep dive.
08:40 Maya Chen: perfect. thanks everyone.
08:45 Liam O'Connell: thanks.
